liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Frozen Logger** (2 reviews): The band's lunacy during this song matched the fun of the audience between the rocks [23][24]
- **Crazy Fingers** (2 reviews): This sparkling performance sounded like the early 1970s band for a few golden moments [23][24]
- **Shakedown Street** (1 review): Gans linked the Frozen Logger to this song, making it one of the reviewer's favorites [31]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-09-07.mtx.chappell.sb26.92184.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 157 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: The transfer process involved multiple digital steps including Cool Edit Pro and FLAC encoding [1]
- **gd85-09-07.oade.georges.17078.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 160 min; rated 4.86/5 by 14 [2]
- **gd85-09-07.schoeps.oade.373.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 158 min; rated 4.14/5 by 7 [3]. Said about its sound: The nicely remastered audience recording brings back the full experience of the concert [23]
- **gd1985-09-07.163915.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 24 songs; 156 min [4]
- **gd85-09-07.sbd.miller.18102.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 151 min; rated 4.21/5 by 24 [14]. Said about its sound: The nicely remastered audience recording brings back the full experience of the concert; Background distortion and strange clown horns give this performance a uniquely Grateful Dead sound [24][27]

## Around the show

- Mickey and Phil played kazoos and horns off stage during this song, creating a riot [28]
- The Red Rocks venue was awesome on a sunny day, making the show fantastic [28]
- The reviewer arrived late after turning around on I-70 due to a bad mood [30]
- The reviewer was dancing with a woman when the band transitioned into this song [33]
- Mickey and Phil played kazoos and slide whistles, while Healy and Owsley did sound effects [7]
- The Frozen Logger was played before the set started, followed by the Star Spangled Banner tuning [7]
- The soundboard recording is considered the better download compared to the audience recordings [31]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-09-07.mtx.chappell.sb26.92184.flac16**: taped by See notes; transferred by Chris Chappell; source: Matrix (SBD/AUD mix) ratio = Phi (the Golden Ratio) - 1.618/1 or 62%/38% [1]. Also: Audio chain includes Schoeps mics, Oade mixer, PCM-F1, DAT, and digital remastering by Doug Oade [1]
- **gd85-09-07.oade.georges.17078.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Doug Oade; transferred by Doug Oade; source: Audience: Schoeps CMC42S [2]. Also: Source uses Schoeps CMC42S and CMC441 mics with Oade power supplies and a custom mixer [2]
- **gd85-09-07.schoeps.oade.373.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Doug Oade; source: Audience: Schoeps CMC42S [3]
- **gd1985-09-07.163915.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME-80 mics > Sony D5M [4]. Also: Oade Schoeps source supplies crowd noise and the beginning of this song, plus a Drums patch [4]
- **gd85-09-07.sbd.miller.18102.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [14]

claims.text: The band's lunacy during this song matched the fun of the audience between the rocks
This sparkling performance sounded like the early 1970s band for a few golden moments
The nicely remastered audience recording brings back the full experience of the concert
The band's lunacy during this song matched the fun of the audience between the rocks
This sparkling performance sounded like the early 1970s band for a few golden moments
The nicely remastered audience recording brings back the full experience of the concert
Background distortion and strange clown horns give this performance a uniquely Grateful Dead sound
Mickey and Phil played kazoos and horns off stage during this song, creating a riot
The Red Rocks venue was awesome on a sunny day, making the show fantastic
The reviewer arrived late after turning around on I-70 due to a bad mood
The soundboard recording is considered the better download compared to the audience recordings
Gans linked the Frozen Logger to this song, making it one of the reviewer's favorites
The reviewer was dancing with a woman when the band transitioned into this song
Audio chain includes Schoeps mics, Oade mixer, PCM-F1, DAT, and digital remastering by Doug Oade
The transfer process involved multiple digital steps including Cool Edit Pro and FLAC encoding
Source uses Schoeps CMC42S and CMC441 mics with Oade power supplies and a custom mixer
Thanks to Michael Hessberg for the master cassette and Charlie Miller for the transfer
Oade Schoeps source supplies crowd noise and the beginning of this song, plus a Drums patch
Mickey and Phil played kazoos and slide whistles, while Healy and Owsley did sound effects
The Frozen Logger was played before the set started, followed by the Star Spangled Banner tuning
